messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.reasoning: We need to calculate sunset time. The tool only calculates sunrise. We can use sunrise to compute sunset? Not directly. We could approximate sunset as sunrise + daylight duration. But we don't have daylight duration. We could use sunrise function to get sunrise time, then approximate sunset by adding 12 hours? That would be inaccurate. We might need to call a different function but none available. We could respond that we cannot compute sunset with given tool. But maybe we can approximate using sunrise and known daylight length? We could approximate daylight length using date and location. But we don't have that data. We could approximate using known formula: daylight length depends on latitude and day of year. We could approximate using approximate formula: daylight hours = 12 + (2/15)*arcsin(sin(23.44°)*sin(2π*(d-81)/365))? Actually formula: daylight hours = 24 - (24/π) * arccos( (sin(φ) * sin(δ) + cos(φ) * cos(δ) * cos(H)) ), where H is hour angle at sunrise. But we don't have δ (solar declination). We could approximate using known approximate formula: daylight hours = 12 + (2/15)*arcsin(tan(φ)*tan(δ)). But we need δ. δ = 23.44° * sin(2π*(d-81)/365). d is day of year. For today (2026-05-19), d=139. So δ ≈ 23.44° * sin(2π*(139-81)/365) = 23.44° * sin(2π*58/365). 58/365 ≈ 0.1589. 2π*0.1589 ≈ 0.999 rad. sin(0.999) ≈ 0.84. So δ ≈ 23.44° * 0.84 ≈ 19.7°. φ for Beijing ≈ 39.9042° N. tan(φ)=tan(39.9°)=0.83. tan(δ)=tan(19.7°)=0.356. tan(φ)*tan(δ)=0.295. arcsin(0.295)=0.299 rad. (2/15)*0.299 rad = 0.0398 rad? Wait units: arcsin returns rad. But formula uses degrees? Actually formula: daylight hours = 12 + (2/15)*arcsin(tan(φ)*tan(δ)). The arcsin result in degrees? Let's convert: arcsin(0.295)=17.1°. Then (2/15)*17.1° = 2.28°. So daylight hours ≈ 12 + 2.28 = 14.28 hours. So daylight ~14h 17min. So if sunrise is at 5:30, sunset ~19:47. But we need actual sunrise. We can call calculate_sunrise for Beijing today. Let's do that.
